== Specification/basic/overloading.tex:291-405

\section{Overloading Resolution}
\seclabel{resolving-overloading}

\note{
Victor: Does this paragraph, other than the last sentence,
really belong in this section?}

To evaluate a given functional call,
it is necessary to determine which functional declaration
to dispatch to.
To do so,
we consider the declarations that are applicable to that call at run time.
If there is exactly one such declaration,
then the call dispatches to that declaration.
If there is no such declaration,
then the call is \emph{undefined}, which is a static error.
(However, see \secref{applicability-with-coercion}
for how coercion may add to the set of applicable declarations.)
If multiple declarations are applicable to the call at run time,
then we choose an arbitrary declaration among the declarations such that
no other applicable declaration is more specific than them.
A declaration with static parameters is applicable to a call at run time, as
to a static call, when some instance of it whose static arguments satisfy
their bounds is applicable to the call, so the declaration to which a call
dispatches may be one that the static call did not select.
A declaration that the static call selected runs at the instance inferred for
the call (\secref{static-arg-inference}); any other declaration runs at the
instance in which each type parameter is the intersection of the upper bounds
placed on it: its declared bound, \TYP{Any} if it has none
(\secref{type-param}), and the bounds that the dynamic types of the arguments
place on it through the parameter types and that the static type of the call
places on it through the return type.
Where the type parameter is a static argument of a parameterized trait in a
parameter type, as \VAR{X} is in \EXP{t\COLON\TYP{Tag}\llbracket{}X\rrbracket},
the value of the argument fixes it, since no value belongs to two
instantiations of one parameterized trait (\secref{trait-types}); where it is
the whole type of a parameter, the dynamic type of the argument is only a
lower bound, and the type parameter is its bound under the static type of the
call.
The type parameters of a declaration that only dispatch reaches are never
instantiated with \TYP{BottomType}, nor with the union of the types of the
arguments.
\revision{revival-dispatch}{The Working Draft of February 2011 did not say at
which instance a declaration with static parameters runs when dispatch reaches
it and the static call selected another.
The rule stated is the one by which the dispatcher of the type group's paper of
2019 instantiates a declaration (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu, ``Polymorphic
Symmetric Multiple Dispatch with Variance'', POPL 2019); the team had assumed
the union of the lower bounds and could not prove it correct.
Both implementations of the revival take the dynamic type of the argument where
the value does not fix the type parameter: the interpreter because it has no
static types, and so no static type of the call to bound the instance, as with
its choice of coercions (\secref{resolving-coercion}); the compiled path because
its dispatcher reads the static arguments of a dispatched declaration from the
value and is not given the static type of the call.
Where the value fixes the type parameter, the two rules give the same instance.
The compiled path's departure is gated as an expected failure (row~538 of the
revival's gap ledger), and the compiled path does not yet run the second
example below (row~496).}



We use the subtype relation to compare parameter types to determine
a more specific declaration.
Formally, a declaration $\f(\Ps)$ is \emph{more specific} than a declaration
$\f(\Qs)$ if $\Ps \strictsubtype \Qs$.  Similarly, a declaration
$\Ps_0.\f(\Ps)$ is more specific than a declaration $\Qs_0.\f(\Qs)$
if $\Ps_0 \strictsubtype \Qs_0$ and $\Ps \strictsubtype \Qs$.
(See \secref{resolving-coercion} for how coercion
changes the definition of ``more specific''.)
Restrictions on the definition of overloaded functionals
(see \chapref{overloaded-declarations})
guarantee that among all applicable declarations,
one is more specific than all the others.
Where declarations have static parameters, they are compared on the parameter
types they declare, each taken over all its instances: a declaration is more
specific than another when the second is applicable to every call to which the
first is applicable, and not the other way round.
Where neither has static parameters, this is the subtype relation above.
No static arguments are inferred for the comparison.
\revision{revival-overloading}{The Working Draft of February 2011 said that
static parameters are inferred as described in \chapref{type-inference} before
the parameter types are compared.
The definition stated is that of the type group's paper of 2011, which checks
it as subtyping of the parameter types read as existential types.}

For example, where \TYP{Shape} comprises the two object types \TYP{Circle}
and \TYP{Square}, of the declarations
%describe[\T extends Shape\](x: T): String = "generic"
%describe(x: Circle): String = "circle"
\begin{Fortress}
\(\VAR{describe}\llbracket{}T \KWD{extends} \TYP{Shape}\rrbracket(x\COLON{}T)\COLON \TYP{String} = \hbox{\rm``\STR{generic}''}\)\\
\(\VAR{describe}(x\COLON \TYP{Circle})\COLON \TYP{String} = \hbox{\rm``\STR{circle}''}\)
\end{Fortress}
the second is more specific than the first, although the first has an instance
whose parameter type is \TYP{Circle}.
The calls \EXP{\VAR{describe}(\TYP{Circle})} and \EXP{\VAR{describe}(s)}, where
\VAR{s} has static type \TYP{Shape} and holds \TYP{Circle}, run the second
declaration, and \EXP{\VAR{describe}(\TYP{Square})} runs the first.
And of the declarations
%grab[\X\](t: Tag[\X\]): Marker[\X\] = Marker[\X\]
%grab(a: Any): Any = Red
\begin{Fortress}
\(\VAR{grab}\llbracket{}X\rrbracket(t\COLON \TYP{Tag}\llbracket{}X\rrbracket)\COLON \TYP{Marker}\llbracket{}X\rrbracket = \TYP{Marker}\llbracket{}X\rrbracket\)\\
\(\VAR{grab}(a\COLON \TYP{Any})\COLON \TYP{Any} = \TYP{Red}\)
\end{Fortress}
where \TYP{Marker} is an object with a type parameter and \TYP{Red} an object
type, the call \EXP{\VAR{grab}(a)}, where \VAR{a} has static type \TYP{Any},
selects the second declaration statically; if \VAR{a} holds a value of an
object type that extends \EXP{\TYP{Tag}\llbracket\TYP{Red}\rrbracket}, the
call dispatches to the first, which is applicable to that value and more
specific, at \EXP{X = \TYP{Red}}, which the value fixes, and returns
\EXP{\TYP{Marker}\llbracket\TYP{Red}\rrbracket}.
\revision{revival-dispatch}{The Working Draft of February 2011 forbade both
pairs of declarations, which differ in their static parameters.}

What the batch takes.** The fixes of section 1, chosen from the inventory's group (a) where the two paths differ or depart from the specification, a program meets the defect, and the fix is small. **Default: so.** Rows 964, 963 and 1044 move to the forks that wait (section 2): each needs an answer first (PRB section 5). Row 1017 stays in group (a) for a later batch: its fix reaches every numeral at a generic declaration, and needs a count first. A program that writes any of these meets today's behaviour.
3. **R1. The node of a numeral with a radix point keeps its digits as written, apostrophes and narrow no-break spaces removed, its leading zeros among them;** `NumeralNumbers.of` counts them; the value is unchanged. **Default: so.** A message that quotes the numeral's text then shows it as written, `00.5`. Way not taken: a separate count kept beside a trimmed text.
4. **W1. A subscript that follows a primary's front evaluates all its indices,** as `forSubscriptExpr` does. **Default: so.**
5. **W2. Each name of a top-level tuple binding reads its element from the temporary,** so the right side runs once. **Default: so.**
6. **S1. An object's dispatch method tests and casts each argument at its own local, whatever the position of `self`.** **Default: so.**
7. **O1. The code generator compiles the modifier `override`, and an object's class holds a method for the override and none for the declarations that it overrides, by the checker's own table of what it keeps from being inherited** (`STypesUtil.providedAndOverridden`), not by a second reading of the rule. **Default: so.** Way not taken: the modifier compiled with the overridden declarations kept in the dispatch, so that `f(B, 17)` runs `A`'s `f`, where walk runs `B`'s.
8. **O2. The checker refuses an `override` that overrides nothing, by the traits chapter's rule (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:680-683`), with walk's words "does not override any inherited declaration"; the worker reports each form that the checker refuses and walk loads (row 693), and copies no gap of walk's.** **Default: so.** Row 694, the checker's choice for numerals at a dotted call, stays open.
9. **A1. An exit out of an atomic block commits the block's transaction, then leaves; a failed commit runs the block again, as at a normal end; an exception other than an exit discards the writes as today.** A nested block's commit hands its writes to the outer transaction, as at a normal end. **Default: so.**
10. **E1. The one library declares `opr EQV(a: Boolean, b: Boolean): Boolean` and its negation `NEQV` (the operators ≡ and ≢) as top-level operators beside `<->`, in its own form for the boolean operators;** the specification and the prelude write them as methods of `Boolean`. **Default: so.** A program that applies `EQV` to two objects of its own then gets a dispatch error, 'Unification error ...', in place of the internal error.
11. **L1. Walk's dotted call of a generic method chooses among the overloads that fit the call's number of arguments.** **Default: so.**
12. **L2. Walk's reading at object arguments compares a tuple result element by element,** as tuple types are covariant. **Default: so.**
13. **L3. Walk's load check refuses a numeral type in a `comprises` clause, with the message that it gives in an `extends` clause.** The three other written forms of item 503 stay as they are. **Default: so.**
14. **M1. An assignment to an object's `var` field from outside calls the setter at the field's declared type, the value cast to it where the cast is needed** (`castToTypeBelow`). **Default: so.**
15. **M2. A call of a functional method of an object that a `comprises` clause lists names a method that the component's class holds,** the overload method written or the call made through the trait. **Default: so.**

(* An object overloads a functional method it inherits, with the self parameter last, by two declarations of its own, one on the meet: each call runs its one applicable or most specific declaration. *)
component XXXFunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast
export Executable

trait N0 end
trait N1 extends N0 end
object N1o extends N1 end
trait S0 end
trait S1 extends S0 end
object S1o extends S1 end
object S0o extends S0 end
trait A
    pick(n: N0, s: S1, self): String = "A"
end
object C extends A
    pick(n: N1, s: S0, self): String = "C0"
    pick(n: N1, s: S1, self): String = "C1"
end

run(): () = do
    println("REACHED")
    assert(pick(N1o, S1o, C), "C1", "the declaration on the meet is the most specific applicable one (overloading.tex, section Overloading Resolution)")
    assert(pick(N1o, S0o, C), "C0", "the one applicable declaration runs (overloading.tex, section Overloading Resolution)")
    println("PASS")
end

end

(* An object that inherits two functional methods of one name with the self parameter second, and covers their meet by two declarations of its own through comprises clauses, runs for each call the most specific declaration (overloading.tex, sections "Meet Rule" and "Overloading Resolution"). *)
component XXXFunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond
export Executable

trait Ka comprises { X1, X2, Ya } end
trait Kb comprises { X1, X2, Yb } end
object X1 extends { Ka, Kb } end
object X2 extends { Ka, Kb } end
object Ya extends Ka end
object Yb extends Kb end
trait P
    mark(x: Ka, self): ZZ32 = 1
end
trait Q
    mark(x: Kb, self): ZZ32 = 2
end
object Pq extends { P, Q }
    mark(x: X1, self): ZZ32 = 3
    mark(x: X2, self): ZZ32 = 4
end

run(): () = do
    println("REACHED")
    assert(mark(X1, Pq), 3, "mark(X1, Pq), self second")
    assert(mark(X2, Pq), 4, "mark(X2, Pq), self second")
    assert(mark(Ya, Pq), 1, "mark(Ya, Pq), self second")
    assert(mark(Yb, Pq), 2, "mark(Yb, Pq), self second")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

(* An object's own functional method with the self parameter second, beside an inherited one over Any, runs only for an argument of its parameter type, and any other argument runs the inherited declaration (overloading.tex, section "Overloading Resolution"). *)
component XXXFunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested
export Executable

trait K end
object Ko extends K end
trait P
    mark(x: Any, self): ZZ32 = 1
end
object Pq extends { K, P }
    mark(x: K, self): ZZ32 = 3
end

    println("REACHED")
    assert(mark(Ko, Pq), 3, "mark(Ko, Pq): the argument has the own declaration's parameter type")

    assert(mark("s", Pq), 1, "mark of a string: only the inherited declaration applies")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

# Climb batch 35's probes: the fixes, reproduced on the base

Run 2026-11-23 between 09:10 and 09:25 UTC, in a worktree of the planner's own, `/home/user/fortress-p35`, seeded from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base42` at `295c215c2c` and removed after. The machine: 4 CPUs, Intel Xeon @ 2.30 GHz, JDK 25.0.4.1, the harness at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`. The programs are in `programs/` beside this note: `programs/tests/` ran under walk through `harness-one.sh`, `programs/compiler_tests/` against the compiler's prelude through `junit.sh` with `ONE_JVM=1`. A walk program here is the plain-named copy of the row's `XXX` test where one exists, so that it fails as the promoted test will; a compiled one has the prefix `P35`, which a rung drops. The inventory that this batch works from is `skill-workarounds.md`, beside this note.

## 1. Under walk, on the base

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/h1 ProjectFortress/tests/RadixPointLeadingZerosWalk.fss \
      ProjectFortress/tests/SubscriptThenSuperscriptWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/TopLevelTupleBindingOnceWalk.fss \
      ProjectFortress/tests/ExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/NumeralBesideTypeParameterWalk.fss \
      ProjectFortress/tests/GenericMethodOverloadArity.fss ProjectFortress/tests/NumeralTypeComprisedWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/NumeralTypeComprisedWalk.test ...

`# harness-one 2026-11-23T09:11:47Z; tree 295c215c2c; nproc=4; ... cache empty`, then `Tests run: 8,  Failures: 8,  Errors: 0`. Each, by its row:

- **Row 960,** `RadixPointLeadingZerosWalk`: 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 2 =/= a ZZ32: 3; literals.tex, section "Literals": 00.5 has three digits'.
- **Row 1,** `SubscriptThenSuperscriptWalk`: 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 11449 =/= a ZZ32: 1075369; two indices, then a superscript'. With one index, a direct run of `P35SubscriptOneIndexWalk.fss` prints `x[5]^2 = 36` for `(x[5])^2`, then stops at the bare `x[5]^2`: 'Failed to find any matching overload, args = (), overload = { ... }'.
- **Row 1026,** `TopLevelTupleBindingOnceWalk`: 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 3 =/= a ZZ32: 1; the right side ran once'.
- **Row 1039,** `ExitOutOfAtomicWalk`: 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 0 =/= a ZZ32: 7; writes within a block that an exit leaves are retained'.
- **Row 1017,** `NumeralBesideTypeParameterWalk`: 'FAIL: J7/0:generic =/= J4/0:nn32'.
- **Row 1057,** `GenericMethodOverloadArity`: 'Cannot find definition for method tk given receiver Two'.
- **Row 981,** `NumeralTypeComprisedWalk` with its `.test`: 'REACHED: a numeral type is in a comprises clause', then 'Missing expected refusal at load'.
- **Row 1044,** a plain copy of `XXXGenericBesidePlainObjectNoReturnTypeWalk` with its `.test` (it overwrote, in the scratch tree only, the team-plain test of the same name, restored after): 'two', then 'Missing expected refusal at load'. Not taken (section 5).

Two more, each in a call of its own:

- **Row 1058,** `GenericBesidePlainTupleReturnWalk`, run as `harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/h3 ...`: refused at load, 'Overloading of pt(a:Dot):(Dot, FortressLibrary.ZZ32) ... and pt[\T extends FortressLibrary.Number\](a:T):(T, FortressLibrary.ZZ32) ...' ('fails the Return Type Rule'), `Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1`.
- **Row 184,** `BooleanEquivalenceWalk`, `t ≡ t` and `t EQV f` for `t: Boolean = true`, `f: Boolean = false`: '** bug! Expect all oprefs to be top level EQV', an `InterpreterBug`, `Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1`.

A program met on the way, already a row: an untyped `x = [1 2 3 4 5 6 7]` in a block stops, 'Can't infer element type for array construction' (row 49); the programs bind `x: ZZ32[7]`.

    The code generator writes each inherited method once into a class and forwards to a body in an api's trait
    
    Climb batch 31, rung M (rows 990, 732 and 571). For a trait's and an
    object's class the code generator gathered the forwarders to inherited
    bodies by a comparison of two domains as schemas over each trait's own
    static parameters, so a generic trait that declared again a method which
    it inherited got the method twice and its class failed as it loaded; and
    it skipped every declaration without a body, an imported api's among
    them, so a body that came through an api's trait that was not first got
    no forwarder and the call died with AbstractMethodError. The class now
    gets each method once, the declaration of the lowest type that declares
    it, compared at the instance that the extends clauses give, and a method
    that an api declares without abstract counts as a body. A functional
    method with self not first is no longer written beside its dispatch
    method. Row 573 is rewritten, and rows 1037 and 1038 are new.

(* Two traits each declare a functional method of one name with the self parameter second of three, and the object extending both declares its own on their meet, narrower than each in a different parameter: the overloading is valid and each call runs its most specific declaration. *)
component FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst
export Executable

trait N0 end
trait N1 extends N0 end
object N1o extends N1 end
trait S0 end
trait S1 extends S0 end
object S1o extends S1 end
trait A
    pick(n: N0, self, s: S1): String = "A"
end
trait B
    pick(n: N1, self, s: S0): String = "B"
end
object C extends { A, B }
    pick(n: N1, self, s: S1): String = "C"
end
object Ao extends A end


run(): () = do
    assert(pick(N1o, C, S1o), "C", "the object that provides both declarations runs its own declaration on their meet (overloading.tex, sections Meet Rule and Overloading Resolution)")
    assert(pick(N1o, Ao, S1o), "A", "an object that provides one declaration runs that declaration (overloading.tex, section Overloading Resolution)")
    println("PASS")
end

end
tests=FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst
link
run
run_out_contains=PASS
tests=FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst
link
tests=FunctionalMethodMeetSelfSecond
compile
link
run

(* Two traits each declare functional methods of one name with the self parameter second, and the object extending both declares its own: the meet is compared without the self parameter wherever it sits, so the overloading is valid. *)
component FunctionalMethodMeetSelfSecond
export Executable

trait A
    pick(n: ZZ32, self): String = "A"
    opr IN(n: ZZ32, self): Boolean = false
end
trait B
    pick(n: ZZ32, self): String = "B"
    opr IN(n: ZZ32, self): Boolean = false
end
object C extends { A, B }
    pick(n: ZZ32, self): String = "C"
    opr IN(n: ZZ32, self): Boolean = true
end
object Ao extends A end

run(): () = do
    assert(pick(3, C), "C", "the object that provides both declarations, self second, runs its own declaration on their meet (overloading.tex, section Meet Rule, the Meet Rule for Functional Methods)")
    assert(pick(3, Ao), "A", "an object that provides one declaration, self second, runs that declaration (overloading.tex, section Overloading Resolution)")
    assert(if 3 IN C then "in" else "out" end, "in", "the object that provides both operator declarations, self second, runs its own declaration on their meet (overloading.tex, section Meet Rule, the Meet Rule for Functional Methods)")
    println("PASS")
end

end

== explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:365-375

## B.7 Overloading

Resolution is split between a shared rewrite and two completely different dispatch mechanisms.

The shared part: `OverloadRewriter` replaces a reference that has several candidates with a reference to a single synthetic name spelled `f{f1,f2,…}` and appends a `_RewriteFnOverloadDecl` declaring it (`compiler/OverloadRewriter.java:74-92`, `OverloadRewriteVisitor.java:110-142`).

On the interpreter path, `BuildTopLevelEnvironments.for_RewriteFnOverloadDecl` (`interpreter/evaluator/BuildTopLevelEnvironments.java:128`) turns that declaration into an `OverloadedFunction`, and the actual selection happens per call, on run-time values, in `OverloadedFunction.bestMatch` (`interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:787`); failure is the familiar "Failed to find any matching overload" (`:795`).

On the compiler path, `CodeGen.for_RewriteFnOverloadDecl` (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:6409`) hands the declaration to `OverloadSet`, which emits one dispatch method per overloaded name, testing argument types from most to least specific (`compiler/OverloadSet.java:1944,1964`).

So the same phase feeds a run-time search in one world and a generated decision tree in the other, and the candidate lists they start from are different (`OverloadRewriteVisitor.java:107`): the interpreter's comes from the disambiguator, the compiler's from the type checker.

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

component_of () {
    # component/api name as declared, which is what `fortress run` wants
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\(component\|api\)[[:space:]]\+\([A-Za-z0-9_.]\+\).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -1
}

run_one () {
    local corpus="$1" path="$2"
    local base name comp crc rrc t0 t1 ct rt
    base=$(basename "$path")
    name="${base%.*}"
    comp=$(component_of "$path")
    [ -n "$comp" ] || comp="$name"

    t0=$(date +%s)
    timeout -k 5 "$COMPILE_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress compile "$path" \
        > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.compile" 2>&1
    crc=$?
    t1=$(date +%s); ct=$((t1-t0))

    rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"
    prune_cache
    echo "=== ladder done $(date -Is), $n files ==="
    disk_guard
}

main "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.
add, rewrite, close and duplicate check the whole line they write; note checks
only what it changes (the notes cell and the row's length), so that a row
failing the template elsewhere still takes a note. A row at its length limit
takes no note: rewrite cuts it back (the rework's decision D4, "each is cut
when next edited", process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md).

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order
  note N TEXT [--check]      adds TEXT to row N's notes, before the row's own
                             "full text: history, row N" marker where it has
                             one, else at their end (notes of `none` are
                             replaced); checks the notes cell and the row's
                             length only, so a failure in another cell does
                             not block it; a row keeps its own cells. With
                             --check it writes nothing: it prints whether
                             TEXT fits, and the characters that the notes
                             (700) and the row (1,200) would have left with

content.content:
For method declarations, we must take into account the self parameter,
as follows:

A \emph{dotted method declaration $\Ps_0.\f(\Ps):\Us$} is a dotted
method declaration with name $f$, where $\Ps_0$ is the trait or object
type in which the declaration appears, $\Ps$ is the parameter type,
and $\Us$ is the return type.  (Note that despite the suggestive
notation, a dotted method declaration does not explicitly list its
self parameter.)

A \emph{functional method declaration $\f(\Ps):\Us$ with self
parameter at $i$} is a functional method declaration with name $f$,
with the parameter \EXP{\mathord{\KWD{self}}} in the $i$th position
of the parameter type $\Ps$, and return type $\Us$.  Note that the static
type of the self parameter is the trait or object trait type in which
the declaration $\f(\Ps):\Us$ occurs.  In the following, we will use
$\Ps_i$ to refer to the $i$th element of $\Ps$.

We elide the return type of a declaration, writing $\f(\Ps)$ and
$\Ps_0.\f(\Ps)$, when the return type is not relevant to the
discussion.
Note that static parameters may appear in the types $\Ps_0$, $\Ps$, and $\Us$.

## What changed and why

The dispatch method of a functional method, in a trait's or an object's class, is an instance method of the receiver's class: self is the receiver, in local 0, and the other arguments follow in their order without self (its descriptor skips self, OverloadSet.java:2565; the forwarding wrapper pushes self as the receiver and then the others, CodeGen.java:3736-3760). `OverloadSet.generateCall` loaded the argument at place `j` of a member's parameters from local `j + offset` for its type test (OverloadSet.java:1538 on the base) and from local `j + firstArgIndex` for the arm's call (OverloadSet.java:1876 on the base), with `firstArg()` 0 for a functional method (OverloadSet.java:2483-2485). That is right only where self is first. With self second or last, the argument before self was read from the local before its own: the first argument from local 0, the receiver. So the type test tested the receiver, and the last arm, which has no test, cast the receiver to the argument's type: a `ClassCastException` where the receiver is not of that type (row 573), and the object's own declaration for every argument where it is (row 1038).

The edit adds `argumentLocal(j, first)`, the local of the argument at place `j`, `j + first` in `OverloadSet` (OverloadSet.java:2357-2363), overridden in `ForTraitOrObject` (OverloadSet.java:2495-2508): for a functional method, an argument before self's place is in the local after its place, `j + 1`, and one after self's place in the local at its place, `j + first` with `first` 0. The type test and the arm's call read it (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1876). For a dotted method (`selfIndex` is `NO_SELF`) and a top-level function the method gives what the two sites gave before. This is fork S1 of the batch (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:449).

The three other sites of the file that read an argument's local are unchanged, each for its reason:

- the inference branch, `ALOAD j` (OverloadSet.java:1846), loads the parameters of a generic arm that `getFunctionToCall` converted to a function with self first, so its locals are at their places; for a functional method no program reaches it, since an object's generic functional method beside a plain one stops the code generator in `getFunctionToCall` (OverloadSet.java:2782, row 724);
- the varargs arm's array, `firstArgIndex + p + j` (OverloadSet.java:2031), takes the arguments after the `p` plain ones, self among them, so it is right wherever self stands among the plain parameters (read, not measured: the compiler's prelude refuses a varargs parameter);
- `generateLeafCall` (OverloadSet.java:1990) has no caller.

## What changed and why

The dispatch method of a functional method, in a trait's or an object's class, is an instance method of the receiver's class: self is the receiver, in local 0, and the other arguments follow in their order without self (its descriptor skips self, OverloadSet.java:2565; the forwarding wrapper pushes self as the receiver and then the others, CodeGen.java:3736-3760). `OverloadSet.generateCall` loaded the argument at place `j` of a member's parameters from local `j + offset` for its type test (OverloadSet.java:1538 on the base) and from local `j + firstArgIndex` for the arm's call (OverloadSet.java:1876 on the base), with `firstArg()` 0 for a functional method (OverloadSet.java:2483-2485). That is right only where self is first. With self second or last, the argument before self was read from the local before its own: the first argument from local 0, the receiver. So the type test tested the receiver, and the last arm, which has no test, cast the receiver to the argument's type: a `ClassCastException` where the receiver is not of that type (row 573), and the object's own declaration for every argument where it is (row 1038).

The edit adds `argumentLocal(j, first)`, the local of the argument at place `j`, `j + first` in `OverloadSet` (OverloadSet.java:2357-2363), overridden in `ForTraitOrObject` (OverloadSet.java:2495-2508): for a functional method, an argument before self's place is in the local after its place, `j + 1`, and one after self's place in the local at its place, `j + first` with `first` 0. The type test and the arm's call read it (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1876). For a dotted method (`selfIndex` is `NO_SELF`) and a top-level function the method gives what the two sites gave before. This is fork S1 of the batch (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:449).

The three other sites of the file that read an argument's local are unchanged, each for its reason:

- the inference branch, `ALOAD j` (OverloadSet.java:1846), loads the parameters of a generic arm that `getFunctionToCall` converted to a function with self first, so its locals are at their places; for a functional method no program reaches it, since an object's generic functional method beside a plain one stops the code generator in `getFunctionToCall` (OverloadSet.java:2782, row 724);
- the varargs arm's array, `firstArgIndex + p + j` (OverloadSet.java:2031), takes the arguments after the `p` plain ones, self among them, so it is right wherever self stands among the plain parameters (read, not measured: the compiler's prelude refuses a varargs parameter);
- `generateLeafCall` (OverloadSet.java:1990) has no caller.

# Rung S: the dispatch method of a functional method whose self is not first

- problem: on the compiled path, where an object overloads an inherited functional method by declarations of its own whose self is not first, a call dies with `ClassCastException` (row 573) or answers the object's declaration for every argument (row 1038), measured by the planner on the base: explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:40
- spec: a functional method's parameter type holds self at its place, and a call runs the most specific declaration applicable to it at run time: Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181 and Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312
- precedent: the layout of a functional method's own locals, the receiver in local 0 and every parameter but self after it in order (`CodeGen.addParams`), which the dispatch method's descriptor already follows (`getSignature(selfIndex)`, OverloadSet.java:2565): ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:3369
- deviation: none; the dispatch method of a dotted method, of a top-level function and of a functional method with self first keeps its bytecode (javap, section "Each program run old against new"): none
- historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2504

One launch worked this rung. The worktree was seeded by the brief's command (exit 0, 3 s) from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base42` (at 295c215c2c, an ancestor of the base 13f4fdea75 with no difference under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`). Commits on `wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch`, cut from 13f4fdea75: c03be68be8 (the three tests promoted, the self-second-of-three case), 630708ad6d (the trait case), 9d9a67df82 (the fix), and the commit of this report.

## What changed and why

The dispatch method of a functional method, in a trait's or an object's class, is an instance method of the receiver's class: self is the receiver, in local 0, and the other arguments follow in their order without self (its descriptor skips self, OverloadSet.java:2565; the forwarding wrapper pushes self as the receiver and then the others, CodeGen.java:3736-3780). `OverloadSet.generateCall` loaded the argument at place `j` of a member's parameters from local `j + offset` for its type test (OverloadSet.java:1538 on the base) and from local `j + firstArgIndex` for the arm's call (OverloadSet.java:1876 on the base), with `firstArg()` 0 for a functional method (OverloadSet.java:2491-2493). That is right only where self is first. With self second or last, the argument before self was read from the local before its own: the first argument from local 0, the receiver. So the type test tested the receiver, and the last arm, which has no test, cast the receiver to the argument's type: a `ClassCastException` where the receiver is not of that type (row 573), and the object's own declaration for every argument where it is (row 1038).

The edit adds `argumentLocal(j, first)`, the local of the argument at place `j`, `j + first` in `OverloadSet` (OverloadSet.java:2357-2363), overridden in `ForTraitOrObject` (OverloadSet.java:2495-2508): for a functional method, an argument before self's place is in the local after its place, `j + 1`, and one after self's place in the local at its place, `j + first` with `first` 0. The type test and the arm's call read it (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1876). For a dotted method (`selfIndex` is `NO_SELF`) and a top-level function the method gives what the two sites gave before. This is fork S1 of the batch (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:449).

The three other sites of the file that read an argument's local are unchanged, each for its reason:

- the inference branch, `ALOAD j` (OverloadSet.java:1846), loads the parameters of a generic arm that `getFunctionToCall` converted to a function with self first, so its locals are at their places; for a functional method no program reaches it, since an object's generic functional method beside a plain one stops the code generator in `getFunctionToCall` (OverloadSet.java:2782, row 724);
- the varargs arm's array, `firstArgIndex + p + j` (OverloadSet.java:2031), takes the arguments after the `p` plain ones, self among them, so it is right wherever self stands among the plain parameters (read, not measured: the compiler's prelude refuses a varargs parameter);
- `generateLeafCall` (OverloadSet.java:1990) has no caller.

`FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` and `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst` print `PASS` in the same run. The build before it: `ant compileAll`, 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL', then the library order, five compiles with exit 0.

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The map gives the compiled path's dispatch to `OverloadSet`, which emits one dispatch method per overloaded name (explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md, "B.7 Overloading"). The rung's section names `ForTraitOrObject` and what `generateCall` emits for it. No earlier commit repaired an argument's local in `OverloadSet.java`: of the revival's commits to the file, only e9bc2ed3e3 (varargs) added a site that reads one, `armCallsVarargsDeclaration`, which is right wherever self stands. The file has five sites that read an argument's local (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1846, :1876, :1990-2018, :2031); the edit changes two, and section "What changed and why" gives the reason for each of the other three. The layout followed is the team's own: `CodeGen.addParams` (CodeGen.java:3369-3375) gives a functional method's body the receiver in local 0 and every parameter but self after it, and `functionalForwardingMethod` (CodeGen.java:3736-3780) calls the method so. `ForTraitOrObject` already holds the other facts of that layout, `loadThisForMethods`, `firstArg()` and `selfIndex()` (OverloadSet.java:2481-2493, :2510-2513), so the override sits beside them.

## What the specification settles

A functional method declaration with self at place `i` has the parameter type `Ps` with self at its `i`th element (Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181), and a call dispatches to the declaration applicable to it at run time that no other applicable one is more specific than (Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312), more specific by the subtype relation on the whole parameter types (:353-358). So each argument is tested at its own place, whatever self's place. Walk runs each call so; the compiled path now does too.

## Each program run old against new

| `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast` | `ClassCastException: ...$Do cannot be cast to ...$N1` | `PASS` |

| `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst` | `ClassCastException: ...$C cannot be cast to ...$N0` | `PASS` |

The full text is committed at explorations/compile-ladder/rung-self-not-first-dispatch/REPORT.md on wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch (c89b2f356b); it is reproduced here word for word.

# Rung S: the dispatch method of a functional method whose self is not first

- problem: on the compiled path, where an object overloads an inherited functional method by declarations of its own whose self is not first, a call dies with `ClassCastException` (row 573) or answers the object's declaration for every argument (row 1038), measured by the planner on the base: explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:40
- spec: a functional method's parameter type holds self at its place, and a call runs the most specific declaration applicable to it at run time: Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181 and Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312
- precedent: the layout of a functional method's own locals, the receiver in local 0 and every parameter but self after it in order (`CodeGen.addParams`), which the dispatch method's descriptor already follows (`getSignature(selfIndex)`, OverloadSet.java:2565): ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:3369
- deviation: none; the dispatch method of a dotted method, of a top-level function and of a functional method with self first keeps its bytecode (javap, section "Each program run old against new"): none
- historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2504

One launch worked this rung. The worktree was seeded by the brief's command (exit 0, 3 s) from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base42` (at 295c215c2c, an ancestor of the base 13f4fdea75 with no difference under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`). Commits on `wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch`, cut from 13f4fdea75: c03be68be8 (the three tests promoted, the self-second-of-three case), 630708ad6d (the trait case), 9d9a67df82 (the fix), and the commit of this report.

## What changed and why

The dispatch method of a functional method, in a trait's or an object's class, is an instance method of the receiver's class: self is the receiver, in local 0, and the other arguments follow in their order without self (its descriptor skips self, OverloadSet.java:2565; the forwarding wrapper pushes self as the receiver and then the others, CodeGen.java:3736-3780). `OverloadSet.generateCall` loaded the argument at place `j` of a member's parameters from local `j + offset` for its type test (OverloadSet.java:1538 on the base) and from local `j + firstArgIndex` for the arm's call (OverloadSet.java:1876 on the base), with `firstArg()` 0 for a functional method (OverloadSet.java:2491-2493). That is right only where self is first. With self second or last, the argument before self was read from the local before its own: the first argument from local 0, the receiver. So the type test tested the receiver, and the last arm, which has no test, cast the receiver to the argument's type: a `ClassCastException` where the receiver is not of that type (row 573), and the object's own declaration for every argument where it is (row 1038).

The edit adds `argumentLocal(j, first)`, the local of the argument at place `j`, `j + first` in `OverloadSet` (OverloadSet.java:2357-2363), overridden in `ForTraitOrObject` (OverloadSet.java:2495-2508): for a functional method, an argument before self's place is in the local after its place, `j + 1`, and one after self's place in the local at its place, `j + first` with `first` 0. The type test and the arm's call read it (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1876). For a dotted method (`selfIndex` is `NO_SELF`) and a top-level function the method gives what the two sites gave before. This is fork S1 of the batch (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:449).

The three other sites of the file that read an argument's local are unchanged, each for its reason:

- the inference branch, `ALOAD j` (OverloadSet.java:1846), loads the parameters of a generic arm that `getFunctionToCall` converted to a function with self first, so its locals are at their places; for a functional method no program reaches it, since an object's generic functional method beside a plain one stops the code generator in `getFunctionToCall` (OverloadSet.java:2782, row 724);
- the varargs arm's array, `firstArgIndex + p + j` (OverloadSet.java:2031), takes the arguments after the `p` plain ones, self among them, so it is right wherever self stands among the plain parameters (read, not measured: the compiler's prelude refuses a varargs parameter);
- `generateLeafCall` (OverloadSet.java:1990) has no caller.

The full text is committed at explorations/compile-ladder/rung-self-not-first-dispatch/REPORT.md on wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch (c89b2f356b); it is reproduced here word for word.

# Rung S: the dispatch method of a functional method whose self is not first

- problem: on the compiled path, where an object overloads an inherited functional method by declarations of its own whose self is not first, a call dies with `ClassCastException` (row 573) or answers the object's declaration for every argument (row 1038), measured by the planner on the base: explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:40
- spec: a functional method's parameter type holds self at its place, and a call runs the most specific declaration applicable to it at run time: Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181 and Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312
- precedent: the layout of a functional method's own locals, the receiver in local 0 and every parameter but self after it in order (`CodeGen.addParams`), which the dispatch method's descriptor already follows (`getSignature(selfIndex)`, OverloadSet.java:2565): ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:3369
- deviation: none; the dispatch method of a dotted method, of a top-level function and of a functional method with self first keeps its bytecode (javap, section "Each program run old against new"): none
- historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2504

One launch worked this rung. The worktree was seeded by the brief's command (exit 0, 3 s) from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base42` (at 295c215c2c, an ancestor of the base 13f4fdea75 with no difference under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`). Commits on `wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch`, cut from 13f4fdea75: c03be68be8 (the three tests promoted, the self-second-of-three case), 630708ad6d (the trait case), 9d9a67df82 (the fix), and the commit of this report.

## What changed and why

The dispatch method of a functional method, in a trait's or an object's class, is an instance method of the receiver's class: self is the receiver, in local 0, and the other arguments follow in their order without self (its descriptor skips self, OverloadSet.java:2565; the forwarding wrapper pushes self as the receiver and then the others, CodeGen.java:3736-3780). `OverloadSet.generateCall` loaded the argument at place `j` of a member's parameters from local `j + offset` for its type test (OverloadSet.java:1538 on the base) and from local `j + firstArgIndex` for the arm's call (OverloadSet.java:1876 on the base), with `firstArg()` 0 for a functional method (OverloadSet.java:2491-2493). That is right only where self is first. With self second or last, the argument before self was read from the local before its own: the first argument from local 0, the receiver. So the type test tested the receiver, and the last arm, which has no test, cast the receiver to the argument's type: a `ClassCastException` where the receiver is not of that type (row 573), and the object's own declaration for every argument where it is (row 1038).

The edit adds `argumentLocal(j, first)`, the local of the argument at place `j`, `j + first` in `OverloadSet` (OverloadSet.java:2357-2363), overridden in `ForTraitOrObject` (OverloadSet.java:2495-2508): for a functional method, an argument before self's place is in the local after its place, `j + 1`, and one after self's place in the local at its place, `j + first` with `first` 0. The type test and the arm's call read it (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1876). For a dotted method (`selfIndex` is `NO_SELF`) and a top-level function the method gives what the two sites gave before. This is fork S1 of the batch (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:449).

The three other sites of the file that read an argument's local are unchanged, each for its reason:

- the inference branch, `ALOAD j` (OverloadSet.java:1846), loads the parameters of a generic arm that `getFunctionToCall` converted to a function with self first, so its locals are at their places; for a functional method no program reaches it, since an object's generic functional method beside a plain one stops the code generator in `getFunctionToCall` (OverloadSet.java:2782, row 724);
- the varargs arm's array, `firstArgIndex + p + j` (OverloadSet.java:2031), takes the arguments after the `p` plain ones, self among them, so it is right wherever self stands among the plain parameters (read, not measured: the compiler's prelude refuses a varargs parameter);
- `generateLeafCall` (OverloadSet.java:1990) has no caller.

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The map gives the compiled path's dispatch to `OverloadSet`, which emits one dispatch method per overloaded name (explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md, "B.7 Overloading"). The rung's section names `ForTraitOrObject` and what `generateCall` emits for it. No earlier commit repaired an argument's local in `OverloadSet.java`: of the revival's commits to the file, only e9bc2ed3e3 (varargs) added a site that reads one, `armCallsVarargsDeclaration`, which is right wherever self stands. The file has five sites that read an argument's local (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1846, :1876, :1990-2018, :2031); the edit changes two, and section "What changed and why" gives the reason for each of the other three. The layout followed is the team's own: `CodeGen.addParams` (CodeGen.java:3369-3375) gives a functional method's body the receiver in local 0 and every parameter but self after it, and `functionalForwardingMethod` (CodeGen.java:3736-3780) calls the method so. `ForTraitOrObject` already holds the other facts of that layout, `loadThisForMethods`, `firstArg()` and `selfIndex()` (OverloadSet.java:2481-2493, :2510-2513), so the override sits beside them.

## What the specification settles

A functional method declaration with self at place `i` has the parameter type `Ps` with self at its `i`th element (Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181), and a call dispatches to the declaration applicable to it at run time that no other applicable one is more specific than (Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312), more specific by the subtype relation on the whole parameter types (:353-358). So each argument is tested at its own place, whatever self's place. Walk runs each call so; the compiled path now does too.

# Rung S (`rung-self-not-first-dispatch`): record lines for the gather

Climb batch 35, run 1, rung S. Branch `wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch`, cut from 13f4fdea75; the fix is 9d9a67df82 on the branch (its hash as the gather lands it goes in the closes below). The detail is in `REPORT.md` beside this file.

## Findings

1. **The compiled dispatch method of a trait's or an object's functional method reads each argument at its own local, wherever self stands.** Holds on the compiled path, against the compiler's prelude, for declarations without static parameters of their own (a generic functional method overloaded beside a plain one stops the code generator first, row 724). The dispatch method is an instance method of the receiver's class: self in local 0, the other arguments after it in their order without self. `OverloadSet.argumentLocal` (ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2357-2363), overridden in `ForTraitOrObject` (OverloadSet.java:2495-2508), gives an argument before self's place the local after its place; the type test (:1538) and the arm's call (:1876) read it. Before, both read local `j` for the argument at place `j`, so with self second or last they read the receiver: a `ClassCastException` (row 573) or the object's own declaration for every argument (row 1038). Evidence: `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh s35final ProjectFortress/compiler_tests <the 46 *FunctionalMethod*.test files>` on 9d9a67df82, 'OK (64 tests)', the four tests below printing 'PASS'; on the base, 'ClassCastException: class FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$C cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$N1', '... FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond$Pq cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond$Ka', 'FAIL:  3 =/= 1; mark(1, Pq): only the inherited declaration applies, though the receiver is a K', '... FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst$C cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst$N0', and in a trait's springboard '... FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$Do cannot be cast to class FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$N1'. Tests: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast` (self last, an object and a trait), `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond` (self second, a cover through `comprises`), `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` (self second, the receiver of the parameter's type), `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst` (self second of three, an argument on each side). The dispatch method of a dotted method, of a top-level function and of a functional method with self first keeps its bytecode (javap of `DispatchSelfFirstProbe$C.pick?0`, old and new identical; REPORT.md, "Each program run old against new"). What it means: an object or trait may overload an inherited functional method with self anywhere; the skill's advice to put self first in such overloads is no longer needed.

2. **A call reaches an object's dispatch method of a functional method where the declaration that the top-level dispatch chooses has a more specific one below it in the object's overload set, as an inherited declaration does.** Measured in the programs of this rung. The top-level dispatch of the name, a static method over the declarations' wrappers with every argument at its own place, chooses by all the arguments; where the chosen declaration is the object's own and has none below it, its body is called at its exact signature (self last: `C`'s own `pick(n: N1, s: S0, self)` has `pick(n: N1, s: S1, self)` below it, so its signature holds a dispatch method; `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst$C`: the body at `pick?1(N1,S1)` beside the dispatch methods `pick?1(N0,S0)` and `pick?1(N0,S1)`, javap on the base). So `pick(n, C, S1o)` with `n: N0 = N1o` ran right on the base, and `pick(N0o, C, S1o)`, which runs `A`'s wrapper and lands on `C`'s dispatch method, died (REPORT.md, "The failing runs and the passing run"). What it means: a test of an object's dispatch method calls a declaration that has a more specific one below it in the object, with an argument that the more specific one does not take.

3. **Row 594's test still fails after the fix, with the same message:** `XXXGenericFunctionalMethodSelfSecond` in the run `s35final` on 9d9a67df82, 'Caused by: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.Object XXXGenericFunctionalMethodSelfSecond$Shape.\=tag?1??Arrow?fortress\|CompilerBuiltin\%Object,fortress\|AnyType\%Any?(long, java.lang.String)'', then 'Saw expected failure (Exit code != 0)'. Its site is not the dispatch method of an overload set: the method is not overloaded. What it means: row 594 stays open, at the site its notes name.

4. **`ProjectFortress/tests/disp2.fss` passes compiled on the base 13f4fdea75 and after the fix,** printing 'f PASS' and 'g PASS', where the baseline ladder records it at `run` with 'f FAIL' (explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/ladder.tsv). It is not among the gate's 85 files (explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-34b/gate/ladder/ladder.tsv). Evidence: the ladder's subset driver (`explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh`, copied into the rung's scratch as the skill's gate.md says) with the subset `tests disp2.fss` on 9d9a67df82, 'tests/disp2.fss crc=0 rrc=0', classified `pass`; on the old code, `old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base42 <caches> compile disp2.fss` then `run disp2`, 'f PASS', 'g PASS'. What it means: an UP move since the baseline that predates this rung; the gate's list could take it.

## FACTS

A new entry under "Landed semantics":

- **The dispatch method of a trait's or an object's functional method reads each argument at its own local, wherever self stands.** The method is an instance method of the receiver's class, self in local 0 and the other arguments after it in their order; `OverloadSet.argumentLocal`, overridden in `ForTraitOrObject`, gives an argument before self's place the local after its place, for the type tests and the casts alike (rows 573 and 1038, fixed). A call reaches the method where the declaration that the top-level dispatch of the name chooses has a more specific one below it in the type, as an inherited one does; a declaration of the type with none below it is called at its exact signature, its body. Not reached: a generic functional method overloaded beside a plain one, on which the code generator stops first (row 724). Tests: `compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested`, `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-self-not-first-dispatch/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why".

F-372 is false in its clause "but an object's dispatch method still tests the receiver in place of the argument, and where the receiver itself has the own declaration's parameter type, a call answers wrongly with no error: with `object Pq extends { K, P }` declaring `mark(x: K, self)` beside `P`'s `mark(x: Any, self)`, `mark(1, Pq)` gives 3 where walk gives 1 (rows 1038 and 573)". It now reads, from "so such a class loads": "so such a class loads, and its dispatch method reads each argument at its own local (rows 573 and 1038, fixed)." Evidence: `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` passes on 9d9a67df82.

- **Row 573**, closed by the fix: `ledger.py close 573 --commit <the fix as landed; 9d9a67df82 on the branch> --test ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast.test`. Its other tests: `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond.test`, `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst.test`.
- **Row 1038**, closed by the fix: `ledger.py close 1038 --commit <the fix as landed; 9d9a67df82 on the branch> --test ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested.test`.
- **Row 594**: no change. Its line with the note "Not at row 573's site: with the dispatch method fixed (climb batch 35), the test dies with this message still." fails the notes limit, 'notes-length: 796 characters; at most 700' (`python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py check --rows` on the row's line with the note), and the row's text stays true; finding 3 holds the fact.
- No new row.

The three `XXX` files that rows 573 and 1038 name (`XXXFunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, `XXXFunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `XXXFunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested`) are renamed without the prefix by `git mv` in c03be68be8; the two closes above take the rows off the landing check's `xxx-gone` list.

## The skill, for the gather

`.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/compiler.md:157` ("Traps of the compiled path": the compiled dispatch method tests the receiver's type where it should test the other argument's, rows 573 and 1038, "Put `self` first in such overloads.") is false after the change.

## Handover line

Climb batch 35, rung S (self not first): the dispatch method of a trait's or an object's functional method reads each argument at its own local (`OverloadSet.argumentLocal`, overridden in `ForTraitOrObject`), so rows 573 and 1038 close with their three tests promoted (`FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast`, with a trait case, `FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested`) and a self-second-of-three case added to `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst`; the 46 functional method tests of the compiler track pass in one JVM; row 594's test still fails at its own site; no stage run, by the brief.

## Revival change

Revival change: none. The change brings the compiled path to what the specification says and walk does: a functional method's parameter type holds self at its place (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181`), and a call runs the most specific declaration applicable to it at run time (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312`); walk runs each of the four test programs to 'PASS' on the base. The team's code generator read the receiver for the argument before self, a defect, not a rule of the language.

The full text is committed at explorations/compile-ladder/rung-self-not-first-dispatch/REPORT.md on wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch (c89b2f356b); it is reproduced here word for word.

# Rung S: the dispatch method of a functional method whose self is not first

- problem: on the compiled path, where an object overloads an inherited functional method by declarations of its own whose self is not first, a call dies with `ClassCastException` (row 573) or answers the object's declaration for every argument (row 1038), measured by the planner on the base: explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:40
- spec: a functional method's parameter type holds self at its place, and a call runs the most specific declaration applicable to it at run time: Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181 and Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312
- precedent: the layout of a functional method's own locals, the receiver in local 0 and every parameter but self after it in order (`CodeGen.addParams`), which the dispatch method's descriptor already follows (`getSignature(selfIndex)`, OverloadSet.java:2565): ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:3369
- deviation: none; the dispatch method of a dotted method, of a top-level function and of a functional method with self first keeps its bytecode (javap, section "Each program run old against new"): none
- historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2504

One launch worked this rung. The worktree was seeded by the brief's command (exit 0, 3 s) from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base42` (at 295c215c2c, an ancestor of the base 13f4fdea75 with no difference under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`). Commits on `wip/rung-self-not-first-dispatch`, cut from 13f4fdea75: c03be68be8 (the three tests promoted, the self-second-of-three case), 630708ad6d (the trait case), 9d9a67df82 (the fix), and the commit of this report.

## What changed and why

The dispatch method of a functional method, in a trait's or an object's class, is an instance method of the receiver's class: self is the receiver, in local 0, and the other arguments follow in their order without self (its descriptor skips self, OverloadSet.java:2565; the forwarding wrapper pushes self as the receiver and then the others, CodeGen.java:3736-3780). `OverloadSet.generateCall` loaded the argument at place `j` of a member's parameters from local `j + offset` for its type test (OverloadSet.java:1538 on the base) and from local `j + firstArgIndex` for the arm's call (OverloadSet.java:1876 on the base), with `firstArg()` 0 for a functional method (OverloadSet.java:2491-2493). That is right only where self is first. With self second or last, the argument before self was read from the local before its own: the first argument from local 0, the receiver. So the type test tested the receiver, and the last arm, which has no test, cast the receiver to the argument's type: a `ClassCastException` where the receiver is not of that type (row 573), and the object's own declaration for every argument where it is (row 1038).

The edit adds `argumentLocal(j, first)`, the local of the argument at place `j`, `j + first` in `OverloadSet` (OverloadSet.java:2357-2363), overridden in `ForTraitOrObject` (OverloadSet.java:2495-2508): for a functional method, an argument before self's place is in the local after its place, `j + 1`, and one after self's place in the local at its place, `j + first` with `first` 0. The type test and the arm's call read it (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1876). For a dotted method (`selfIndex` is `NO_SELF`) and a top-level function the method gives what the two sites gave before. This is fork S1 of the batch (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:449).

The three other sites of the file that read an argument's local are unchanged, each for its reason:

- the inference branch, `ALOAD j` (OverloadSet.java:1846), loads the parameters of a generic arm that `getFunctionToCall` converted to a function with self first, so its locals are at their places; for a functional method no program reaches it, since an object's generic functional method beside a plain one stops the code generator in `getFunctionToCall` (OverloadSet.java:2782, row 724);
- the varargs arm's array, `firstArgIndex + p + j` (OverloadSet.java:2031), takes the arguments after the `p` plain ones, self among them, so it is right wherever self stands among the plain parameters (read, not measured: the compiler's prelude refuses a varargs parameter);
- `generateLeafCall` (OverloadSet.java:1990) has no caller.

## The failing runs and the passing run

Before the first build of the edit, on the seeded base build's classes, the promoted tests through the harness (`junit.sh` with `ONE_JVM=1`, four threads; the machine: 4 CPUs, Intel Xeon @ 2.30 GHz, JDK 25.0.4.1). The first call echoed:

`FunctionalMethodCoverSelfSecond`, `FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested` and `FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst` print `PASS` in the same run. The build before it: `ant compileAll`, 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL', then the library order, five compiles with exit 0.

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The map gives the compiled path's dispatch to `OverloadSet`, which emits one dispatch method per overloaded name (explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md, "B.7 Overloading"). The rung's section names `ForTraitOrObject` and what `generateCall` emits for it. No earlier commit repaired an argument's local in `OverloadSet.java`: of the revival's commits to the file, only e9bc2ed3e3 (varargs) added a site that reads one, `armCallsVarargsDeclaration`, which is right wherever self stands. The file has five sites that read an argument's local (OverloadSet.java:1538, :1846, :1876, :1990-2018, :2031); the edit changes two, and section "What changed and why" gives the reason for each of the other three. The layout followed is the team's own: `CodeGen.addParams` (CodeGen.java:3369-3375) gives a functional method's body the receiver in local 0 and every parameter but self after it, and `functionalForwardingMethod` (CodeGen.java:3736-3780) calls the method so. `ForTraitOrObject` already holds the other facts of that layout, `loadThisForMethods`, `firstArg()` and `selfIndex()` (OverloadSet.java:2481-2493, :2510-2513), so the override sits beside them.

## What the specification settles

A functional method declaration with self at place `i` has the parameter type `Ps` with self at its `i`th element (Specification/basic/overloading.tex:175-181), and a call dispatches to the declaration applicable to it at run time that no other applicable one is more specific than (Specification/basic/overloading.tex:298-312), more specific by the subtype relation on the whole parameter types (:353-358). So each argument is tested at its own place, whatever self's place. Walk runs each call so; the compiled path now does too.

## Each program run old against new

Compiled with the old code (`explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base42 tmp/.../old-caches compile P.fss`, then `run P`) and with the fix (`bin/fortress compile` and `run` with a private caches folder), on 9d9a67df82:

| `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast` | `ClassCastException: ...$Do cannot be cast to ...$N1` | `PASS` |

## Points to report

- The dispatch method as fixed: which local each type test and cast reads. Self first: the argument at place `j` in local `j`, unchanged (`DispatchSelfFirstProbe$C.pick?0`, identical bytecode). Self second: the argument before self in local 1 (`FunctionalMethodSelfSecondReceiverTested$Pq.mark?1`), and with three parameters the one after self in local 2 (`FunctionalMethodMeetNarrowedSelfNotFirst$C.pick?1`). Self last: the arguments at places 0 and 1 in locals 1 and 2 (`FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast$C.pick?2`, and the trait's springboard `$D$DefaultTraitMethods.pick?2`). The receiver is read from local 0 only as the arm's call target. Evidence: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:2504-2508, :1538, :1876, and the javap lines above. - The files edited, for STAGE_BLIND: section "The stages, and the files for STAGE_BLIND". And `FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast.fss`, a promoted test, gains the trait case (ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodOverloadSelfLast.fss:19-23, :27-28). Reversible.

No step taken cannot be undone, and none acts against a decision on record.

## Decisions
